title: Training Runs
description: Discover saved classifier runs, overlay train and validation curves, inspect fold variability, and connect performance differences to settings and environment drift.
objectives: Find complete and incomplete training runs without hiding missing curves or settings.
Compare validation accuracy and loss while keeping each run on its own epoch axis.
Audit best versus last epochs, cross-validation spread, and bucketed settings differences.
prerequisite: One or more spaCR model folders containing train.csv and validation.csv logs, with settings snapshots when configuration comparison is required.

scenes.narration: Training Runs is a read-only quality-control screen. It overlays saved train and validation curves and places the settings diff beside them; it never retrains a model or changes a run on disk.
scenes.speech_text: Training Runs is a read only quality control screen. It overlays saved train and validation curves and places the settings diff beside them; it never retrains a model or changes a run on disk.

scenes.narration: Choose the folder that contains model trees, or any parent above several projects, then click Scan. The transferred microscopy data has no saved training curves, so this tutorial clearly uses synthetic spaCR-format logs while exercising the real parser and interface.
scenes.speech_text: Choose the folder that contains model trees, or any parent above several projects, then click Scan. The transferred microscopy data has no saved training curves, so this tutorial clearly uses synthetic spacer format logs while exercising the real parser and interface.

scenes.narration: The scan finds a twenty-epoch baseline, a twenty-five-epoch tuned run, a three-fold cross-validated run, and an intentionally incomplete checkpoint. Missing settings and curves are reported in amber rather than silently discarded, while valid runs remain usable.
scenes.speech_text: The scan finds a twenty epoch baseline, a twenty five epoch tuned run, a three fold cross validated run, and an intentionally incomplete checkpoint. Missing settings and curves are reported in amber rather than silently discarded, while valid runs remain usable.

scenes.narration: Tick the twenty-epoch baseline. Each row names its model, channels, epoch count, folds, and important recovered settings so the selection remains traceable.
scenes.speech_text: Tick the twenty epoch baseline. Each row names its model, channels, epoch count, folds, and important recovered settings so the selection remains traceable.

scenes.narration: Tick the twenty-five-epoch tuned run as the second comparison. Runs of different length are not truncated or padded; every curve retains its true epoch axis.
scenes.speech_text: Tick the twenty five epoch tuned run as the second comparison. Runs of different length are not truncated or padded; every curve retains its true epoch axis.

scenes.narration: Metric chooses a recorded column such as accuracy, loss, precision-recall area, or class accuracy. Folds controls whether cross-validation appears per fold, as mean plus or minus one standard deviation, or both.
scenes.speech_text: Metric chooses a recorded column such as accuracy, loss, precision recall area, or class accuracy. Folds controls whether cross validation appears per fold, as mean plus or minus one standard deviation, or both.

scenes.narration: Click Overlay selected. Dashed lines are training splits and solid lines are validation splits; a rising train curve above a declining validation curve indicates overfitting, not a better model.
scenes.speech_text: Click Overlay selected. Dashed lines are training splits and solid lines are validation splits; a rising train curve above a declining validation curve indicates overfitting, not a better model.

scenes.narration: The tuned validation curve reaches about zero point eight five five before ending near zero point eight four five; the baseline peaks near zero point seven eight six and ends near zero point seven five. The table links that difference to batch size, epochs, learning rate, and source, while worker count is separated as environment drift.

The table links that difference to batch size, epochs, learning rate, and source, while worker count is separated as environment drift.

scenes.narration: Click a curve to identify its run and split instead of relying only on color. The selected series is resolved back to its folder and per-epoch measurements.
scenes.speech_text: Click a curve to identify its run and split instead of relying only on color. The selected series is resolved back to its folder and per epoch measurements.

scenes.narration: The detail line shows the baseline validation series, its epoch range, last accuracy zero point seven four nine six at epoch twenty, and best accuracy zero point seven eight six at epoch fifteen. The best value is labeled optimistic because the same curve selected that epoch.
scenes.speech_text: The detail line shows the baseline validation series, its epoch range, last accuracy zero point seven four nine six at epoch twenty, and best accuracy zero point seven eight six at epoch fifteen. The best value is labeled optimistic because the same curve selected that epoch.

scenes.narration: Open Metric and choose loss. Comparing several metrics prevents a selection based on one flattering endpoint.
scenes.speech_text: Open Metric and choose loss. Comparing several metrics prevents a selection based on one flattering endpoint.

scenes.narration: Loss uses the same runs and settings diff. Here training loss continues downward while validation loss turns upward, making the late overfitting visible from a second measurement rather than accuracy alone.
scenes.speech_text: Loss uses the same runs and settings diff. Here training loss continues downward while validation loss turns upward, making the late overfitting visible from a second measurement rather than accuracy alone.

scenes.narration: Now compare the tuned run with the three-fold run and choose mean plus or minus standard deviation. This summarizes cross-validation without pretending its mean is a single observed run.
scenes.speech_text: Now compare the tuned run with the three fold run and choose mean plus or minus standard deviation. This summarizes cross validation without pretending its mean is a single observed run.

scenes.narration: The blue band is plus or minus one standard deviation across three folds. The mean validation curve ends near zero point eight three, while the band exposes fold-to-fold uncertainty that a single line would conceal.
scenes.speech_text: The blue band is plus or minus one standard deviation across three folds. The mean validation curve ends near zero point eight three, while the band exposes fold to fold uncertainty that a single line would conceal.

scenes.narration: Choose per fold when individual fold behavior matters. This is especially useful for spotting one unstable split or a tail supported by fewer folds after early stopping.
scenes.speech_text: Choose per fold when individual fold behavior matters. This is especially useful for spotting one unstable split or a tail supported by fewer folds after early stopping.

scenes.narration: Per-fold mode draws every train and validation series with run, split, and fold in the legend. Use validation behavior, fold stability, held-out evaluation, and the settings audit together; Training Runs compares evidence but does not declare a scientifically reproducible winner by itself.
